name: AECi — Algolia orphan sweep capped
message:
The daily 09:00 UTC orphan sweep (AECI-266, §23.1) refused to delete an unexpectedly large set of orphan objects from an Algolia index — more than the safety cap allows (≤50 objects and ≤20% of an index per pass). This is the guard against a misconfigured/empty promoted-id read nuking a live search index, so it does NOT auto-purge; the orphans stay searchable (404-on-click) until an operator confirms and forces the purge. The alert is split `by {index}` — the value is the orphan count refused. Read the `source:algolia-drift-cron` log `aeci.algolia.orphans_removed on <env>` (it names the capped index) and verify the count is legitimate before forcing `db:reconcile-algolia-drift -- --env <env> --apply --force` (production also needs --allow-production).

Note: this monitor deliberately does NOT use notify_no_data — `orphans_skipped_cap` is absent on a healthy run (it is emitted only when the cap fires), so no-data here would be a constant false alarm. The per-run heal volume is the companion gauge `aeci.algolia.orphans_removed` (0 on a clean run).

Runbook: https://github.com/the-wbs-project/aec-integrations/blob/main/docs/RUNBOOKS.md#algolia-index-drift
